findings.title: Concurrency test never joins the reader and can miss the race
findings.body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a non-daemon reader that calls groups() in a loop, but never waits for that thread to enter the loop or to finish. deletedAll is set true immediately after the deletes and caughtExceptions is asserted on the next line, so the assertion can run before any list call has started or before an in-flight list has recorded its exception. A regression of the original NPE can therefore pass CI. There is also no finally that stops and joins the thread: if group.remove() throws before deletedAll.set(true), the reader stays in while (!deletedAll.get()) forever, keeps issuing admin requests against the shared realm for the rest of the suite, and can hang JVM shutdown because the thread is not a daemon. The same managedRealm.admin() client is used from both threads, so a client-side concurrency failure is also treated as a product failure. Start the reader behind a latch, delete only after it has begun, and in a finally set the stop flag and join with a timeout before asserting.

findings.title: Missing delegate makes getSubGroupsCount return null
findings.body: When the cached group has already been deleted, getSubGroupsCount returns null instead of a count. GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount copies that value straight into GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount, so a list request that races with a delete can return 200 with a group whose subGroupCount is null. Other GroupModel implementations do not do this: a subgroup count query returns 0 when the parent row is gone, and null is also how the admin API signals that the count was not requested. Callers that unbox the Long (comparisons, arithmetic, longValue()) still NPE, so the crash is moved out of this method rather than removed. Return 0L when modelSupplier.get() is null.

findings.title: Paged subgroup streams still NPE if the group was deleted
findings.body: The null-delegate race is only handled in getSubGroupsCount. The paged overloads still dereference the lazy delegate unconditionally: getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) at line 268 all do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...). If the group was removed after the CachedGroup was loaded, modelSupplier.get() returns null and these methods throw NullPointerException. Those overloads back the admin children API (search and pagination), so delete-while-list still returns 500 on that endpoint. Guard the null delegate the same way and return Stream.empty() instead of chaining the call.
